types.necessity: L1.identity requires that a customer be recognized as the same customer across changes; the identity mutation role names exactly this: the value that says which thing a row is about, unchanged by a mere change to the customer.
types.parallel_assumption: Customer numbers are unique to one customer and are never reused for a different customer.
types.review_trigger: business reuses or reassigns customer numbers

types.necessity: L1.identity requires that an account be recognized as the same account across changes; the identity mutation role names exactly this: the value that says which thing a row is about, unchanged by a mere change to the account.
types.parallel_assumption: Account numbers are unique to one account and are never reused for a different account.
types.review_trigger: business reuses or reassigns account numbers

types.necessity: L1.history requires keeping 'the moment [a change] took effect' for every statement; L1.as-of requires answering any as-of question with 'the latest [statement] that took effect at or before it', which requires each statement to carry its own effective moment as a fact of that one statement.
types.parallel_assumption: A statement's effective moment does not change after the statement exists; only a later statement is added beside it, per L1.history.
types.review_trigger: business says a statement's effective moment can be revised in place rather than superseded by a later statement

types.necessity: L1.current-version defines 'the current statement' as the one with no later statement, and requires exactly one per customer or account; this is a fact about each statement individually, computed from the entity's own statements.
types.parallel_assumption: Statements for one identity are totally ordered by effective time, so 'no later statement' is well-defined.
types.review_trigger: business allows more than one concurrently current statement per customer or account

types.necessity: L1.owner-standing requires that an account's standing include its owner's standing at the same moment; each account statement must therefore carry, as one of its own facts, which customer it is owned by.
types.parallel_assumption: An account's owning customer is a single value per statement; the clause does not state this reference is fixed for the account's lifetime, so it is not treated as frozen (see the rejected frozen-role step below).
types.review_trigger: business states an account can have more than one owning customer, or none, at some moment

types.necessity: Considered because the received action and status codes (ACTV/INAC, tier, tax status) are readily decodable and a status-bearing statement is a common shape for this kind of history.
types.rejected_because: L1.history requires keeping the fact that a change happened to a customer or account and the moment it took effect; it does not say what business content each statement carries. None of this job's clauses (L1.identity, L1.history, L1.as-of, L1.current-version, L1.owner-standing, L1.constructed-scenarios) state that a statement carries a status, tier, or tax-status fact. sources-v1.json states what codes like ACTV/INAC mean, but interpreting a code's meaning is not the same as deciding a statement carries it; that decision is policy and comes only from the Sketch, which is silent here. Filed as a question for authority instead of invented.
types.parallel_assumption: Not applicable to a rejected derivation; recorded to make the temptation and its refusal visible to the next Developer and reviewer.
types.review_trigger: business (or an accepted answer to the filed question) states that a statement carries status, tier, or tax-status content

entities.grain: one row per dated statement about one customer, identified by customer_id
entities.necessity: L1.identity requires a customer be recognized as the same customer across changes; L1.history requires every change to a customer be kept as a new dated statement beside the earlier ones, never overwritten; L1.as-of requires that any question about a customer be answerable as of a moment by the statement in effect then; L1.current-version requires exactly one current statement per customer. A versioned, identity-keyed entity is the structure that satisfies all four at once.
entities.parallel_assumption: Customer statements for one customer_id can be given a determinate effective moment and placed in a total order, so 'the latest statement at or before a moment' and 'no later statement' are both well-defined; this holds today for historical-load and constructed-scenario sourced statements (see hole.change-effective-time for incremental sources).
entities.review_trigger: business states a customer statement carries content beyond identity, effective time, and current-ness, or that customer history is not append-only

attributes.name: customer_id
attributes.necessity: L1.identity names the customer number as the thing that says which customer a statement is about; without it, statements about different customers could not be told apart or recognized as the same one across changes.
attributes.parallel_assumption: The brokerage's customer number is stable and never reassigned to a different customer.
attributes.review_trigger: business reuses or reassigns customer numbers

attributes.name: effective_from
attributes.necessity: L1.history requires that each statement carry the moment it took effect; L1.as-of requires locating the latest statement that took effect at or before a queried moment, which is impossible without each statement recording its own effective moment.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Each customer statement's effective moment is a single point in time, and statements for one customer_id are totally ordered by it.
attributes.review_trigger: business says an effective moment can be plural or tied and broken by something other than time

attributes.name: current_flag

derivation.rule: true exactly when no other statement with the same customer_id has a later effective_from; false otherwise

attributes.necessity: L1.current-version defines the current statement as 'the one with no later statement' and requires exactly one per customer; a flag computed from the entity's own statements is the direct, checkable expression of that definition.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Statements for one customer_id are totally ordered by effective_from, so 'no later statement' is unambiguous.
attributes.review_trigger: business allows more than one concurrently current statement per customer

entities.grain: one row per dated statement about one account, identified by account_id
entities.necessity: L1.identity requires an account be recognized as the same account across changes; L1.history requires every change to an account be kept as a new dated statement beside the earlier ones, never overwritten; L1.as-of requires that any question about an account be answerable as of a moment by the statement in effect then; L1.current-version requires exactly one current statement per account. A versioned, identity-keyed entity is the structure that satisfies all four at once.
entities.parallel_assumption: Account statements for one account_id can be given a determinate effective moment and placed in a total order, so 'the latest statement at or before a moment' and 'no later statement' are both well-defined; this holds today for historical-load and constructed-scenario sourced statements (see hole.change-effective-time for incremental sources).
entities.review_trigger: business states an account statement carries content beyond identity, effective time, and current-ness, or that account history is not append-only

attributes.name: account_id
attributes.necessity: L1.identity names the account number as the thing that says which account a statement is about; without it, statements about different accounts could not be told apart or recognized as the same one across changes.
attributes.parallel_assumption: The brokerage's account number is stable and never reassigned to a different account.
attributes.review_trigger: business reuses or reassigns account numbers

attributes.name: effective_from
attributes.necessity: L1.history requires that each statement carry the moment it took effect; L1.as-of requires locating the latest statement that took effect at or before a queried moment, which is impossible without each statement recording its own effective moment.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Each account statement's effective moment is a single point in time, and statements for one account_id are totally ordered by it.
attributes.review_trigger: business says an effective moment can be plural or tied and broken by something other than time

attributes.name: current_flag

derivation.rule: true exactly when no other statement with the same account_id has a later effective_from; false otherwise

attributes.necessity: L1.current-version defines the current statement as 'the one with no later statement' and requires exactly one per account; a flag computed from the entity's own statements is the direct, checkable expression of that definition.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Statements for one account_id are totally ordered by effective_from, so 'no later statement' is unambiguous.
attributes.review_trigger: business allows more than one concurrently current statement per account

attributes.name: customer_id
attributes.note: Not populated when the statement is sourced from ce.account_changes (constructed scenario), which carries no customer/owner identifier. No clause in this job's list establishes that an omitted owner reference carries forward from the account's previous statement, so it is left absent rather than invented.
attributes.necessity: L1.owner-standing requires that an account's standing include its owner's standing at the same moment; expressing that requires each account statement to name which customer it is owned by, so the two entities can be joined at the same as-of moment.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Each account is owned by exactly one customer at a time, per the received action rows that carry ca_id and c_id together; no clause states this can be plural or absent.
attributes.review_trigger: business states an account can have more than one owning customer, or none, at some moment

handoffs.necessity: L1.identity requires recognizing which customer a statement is about; the historical action rows carry the customer number on every action, so it is handed off directly as the identity value.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: c_id in CustomerMgmt actions is the same customer number used everywhere else in the received records.
handoffs.review_trigger: the historical load stops carrying c_id on every action row

handoffs.necessity: L1.history and L1.as-of both require each statement to carry the moment it took effect; action_ts is the action's own recorded moment, so it is handed off directly as the effective time.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: action_ts states the action's own effective moment, not merely when it was recorded into the file.
handoffs.review_trigger: action_ts is found to be a load or recording time rather than the action's own effective moment

handoffs.necessity: L1.identity requires recognizing which account a statement is about; NEW, ADDACCT, UPDACCT, and CLOSEACCT rows all carry the account number.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: ca_id is the same account number used everywhere else in the received records.
handoffs.review_trigger: an account-subject action stops carrying ca_id

handoffs.necessity: L1.owner-standing requires each account statement to carry which customer owns it; NEW, ADDACCT, UPDACCT, and CLOSEACCT rows carry ca_id and c_id together, so the owning customer is handed off directly.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: c_id on an account-subject action names that same action's account's owning customer, not some other customer.
handoffs.review_trigger: an account-subject action is found to carry c_id for a customer other than the account's owner

handoffs.necessity: L1.history and L1.as-of both require each statement to carry the moment it took effect; action_ts is the action's own recorded moment, so it is handed off directly as the effective time.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: action_ts states the action's own effective moment, not merely when it was recorded into the file.
handoffs.review_trigger: action_ts is found to be a load or recording time rather than the action's own effective moment

handoffs.necessity: L1.constructed-scenarios permits a labeled constructed scenario to change something the received records already know; carrying its account_id into the same identity attribute is what lets it be recognized as about an account the records already have.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: account_id in ce.account_changes always names an account already present in the received records, per the clause's own restriction.
handoffs.review_trigger: a constructed scenario is found to introduce an account_id absent from the received records

handoffs.necessity: A constructed statement needs the same effective-time role as a received one to be placed in the account's history; action_at is ce.account_changes' own stated moment.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: action_at is the constructed scenario's own effective moment, on the same footing as action_ts for received actions.
handoffs.review_trigger: action_at is found to be something other than the constructed scenario's own effective moment

handoffs.necessity: Same identity role as the historical handoff, for incremental customer change records.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: c_id in incremental Customer.txt records is the same customer number used elsewhere in the received records.
handoffs.note: Deferred, not rejected: c_id is a valid identity value, but this record cannot be placed as a statement without an effective time, which raw.customer_cdc does not carry (see hole.change-effective-time).

handoffs.necessity: Same identity role as the historical handoff, for incremental account change records.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: ca_id in incremental Account.txt records is the same account number used elsewhere in the received records.
handoffs.note: Deferred, not rejected: ca_id is a valid identity value, but this record cannot be placed as a statement without an effective time, which raw.account_cdc does not carry (see hole.change-effective-time).

handoffs.necessity: Same owner-reference role as the historical handoff, for incremental account change records.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: c_id in incremental Account.txt records names that same record's account's owning customer, not some other customer.
handoffs.note: Deferred, not rejected: c_id is a valid owner reference, but the account row it belongs to cannot be placed as a statement without an effective time, which raw.account_cdc does not carry (see hole.change-effective-time).

handoffs.necessity: L1.history and L1.as-of require an effective moment for every statement; batch_date is the only time-like field incremental customer records carry.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: No assumption is asserted here; batch_date's suitability as an effective moment is exactly the open question named in hole.change-effective-time.
handoffs.note: batch_date is the loader's ingestion date, not a business-stated moment the change took effect. Treating it as the effective moment would answer hole.change-effective-time by invention rather than by business decision, which is forbidden. Deferred pending that hole.

handoffs.necessity: L1.history and L1.as-of require an effective moment for every statement; batch_date is the only time-like field incremental account records carry.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: No assumption is asserted here; batch_date's suitability as an effective moment is exactly the open question named in hole.change-effective-time.
handoffs.note: batch_date is the loader's ingestion date, not a business-stated moment the change took effect. Treating it as the effective moment would answer hole.change-effective-time by invention rather than by business decision, which is forbidden. Deferred pending that hole.

invariants.statement: For each customer_id, exactly one logical.customer statement has current_flag = true.
invariants.necessity: L1.current-version states there is exactly one current statement per customer; this is the direct, checkable form of that requirement, and matches the job's own feedback line: 'one current statement per customer and per account.'
invariants.parallel_assumption: Statements for one customer_id are totally ordered by effective_from.
invariants.review_trigger: business allows more than one concurrently current statement per customer

invariants.statement: For each account_id, exactly one logical.account statement has current_flag = true.
invariants.necessity: L1.current-version states there is exactly one current statement per account; this is the direct, checkable form of that requirement, and matches the job's own feedback line: 'one current statement per customer and per account.'
invariants.parallel_assumption: Statements for one account_id are totally ordered by effective_from.
invariants.review_trigger: business allows more than one concurrently current statement per account

invariants.statement: No two logical.customer statements for the same customer_id share an effective_from, and for any as-of moment exactly one statement -- the one with the latest effective_from at or before that moment -- answers the question.
invariants.necessity: Matches the job's feedback line 'statements of one thing do not overlap; any as-of question has exactly one answer', which is L1.history's append-only rule combined with L1.as-of's lookup rule.
invariants.parallel_assumption: effective_from values for one customer_id are distinct and totally ordered.
invariants.review_trigger: two statements for the same customer_id are found with the same effective_from

invariants.statement: No two logical.account statements for the same account_id share an effective_from, and for any as-of moment exactly one statement -- the one with the latest effective_from at or before that moment -- answers the question.
invariants.necessity: Matches the job's feedback line 'statements of one thing do not overlap; any as-of question has exactly one answer', which is L1.history's append-only rule combined with L1.as-of's lookup rule.
invariants.parallel_assumption: effective_from values for one account_id are distinct and totally ordered.
invariants.review_trigger: two statements for the same account_id are found with the same effective_from

invariants.statement: For any as-of moment t, the logical.account statement in effect at t, together with the logical.customer statement in effect at t for that account's customer_id, together answer how the account stood at t.
invariants.necessity: Matches the job's feedback line 'an account's as-of answer carries its customer's as-of answer', which is exactly L1.owner-standing's text: 'When the brokerage says how an account stood at a moment, that includes how its customer stood at that same moment.'
invariants.parallel_assumption: An account's customer_id reference is available for the moment being asked about (see hole.change-effective-time for when it is not).
invariants.review_trigger: business says an account's standing can be reported without its customer's standing at the same moment

invariants.statement: Any logical.account statement sourced from ce.account_changes carries its provenance label and is never merged with received-record-sourced statements without that label; such a statement's account_id is always one already present among received-record statements, never a new one.
invariants.necessity: Directly restates L1.constructed-scenarios: labeled as constructed wherever it appears and never mixed into the received records; a constructed scenario never introduces a customer, account, or trade the brokerage does not have.
invariants.parallel_assumption: ce.account_changes rows carry a provenance field distinguishing them from received records, and every constructed account_id has a corresponding received-record statement.
invariants.review_trigger: a constructed scenario is found without a provenance label, or introducing an account_id absent from received records

sufficiency_groups.coverage_claim: Both entities are declared as versioned histories keyed by their stable identifiers (L1.identity), keep one row per dated statement without overwriting earlier ones (L1.history), carry the effective moment that lets any as-of question be answered as the latest statement at or before it (L1.as-of), and carry a current flag computed so that exactly one statement per identity is current (L1.current-version); the invariants check uniqueness of the current statement and that statements of one identity do not overlap or leave an as-of question with more than one answer.
sufficiency_groups.gap: L1.hole.change-effective-time (incremental-sourced customer and account changes carry no effective time of their own, so they cannot yet be placed as statements; only historical-load and constructed-scenario sourced statements are currently projectable)

sufficiency_groups.coverage_claim: The account entity carries, per statement, the identifier of the customer that owns it, sourced from the historical action rows that carry ca_id and c_id together; the invariant checks that an account's as-of standing is reported together with its customer's as-of standing at the same moment, which is exactly what L1.owner-standing requires.
sufficiency_groups.gap: L1.hole.change-effective-time (the incremental-sourced owner reference cannot yet be placed as a statement, for the same reason as sg.versioned-standing)

sufficiency_groups.coverage_claim: The only constructed-scenario source in scope for this job (ce.account_changes) is handed off solely into the account entity's identity and effective-time attributes, kept separate from received-record handoffs; the invariant checks a constructed statement's account_id is always one the received records already have and stays labeled -- exactly what L1.constructed-scenarios requires.

holes.question: For incremental customer and account change records (Customer.txt/Account.txt), does a change take effect at the file's batch date, or at some other moment the business can name? Until answered, incremental-sourced customer and account statements, and the incremental-sourced account-owner reference, are carried as deferred and are not placed in the versioned history.

When a customer's standing changes, does every account of that customer also get a new statement at that same moment, or only the customer? This model does not synthesize a new account statement from a customer-only change; the owner-standing invariant is satisfied by joining each entity's own as-of answer rather than by assuming synchronized rows, so it holds under either answer, but the answer still determines whether an upstream step must produce additional account statements.

Incremental account and customer change records can carry cdc_flag = D (deleted). What does a deleted account or customer record mean for its history, its current statement, and its owner-standing? This model does not interpret D-flagged rows; it is currently moot for this job only because all incremental customer/account sourcing is already deferred under hole.change-effective-time, but the two holes are independent.

questions_for_authority: For job ownership-history, none of its clauses (L1.identity, L1.history, L1.as-of, L1.current-version, L1.owner-standing, L1.constructed-scenarios) state what a customer statement or an account statement carries as business content beyond its identity, its effective time, and whether it is the current one. Does a customer or account statement carry any further fact (for example a status, a tier, a tax status, a name), and if so, which fact and under which clause? Until answered, this model's customer and account statements carry identity, effective time, and current-flag only.
